cautionOverrides.from: French les is plural for both masculine and feminine; it does not preserve the Spanish los/las contrast. In “J’ai besoin des clés,” des is required after de; les later replaces clés. The final question uses l’ for an unspecified singular item; the English source does not identify its gender.
cautionOverrides.to: French les replaces plural direct objects of any gender. In “J’ai besoin des clés,” des follows the need expression, while les later replaces clés. The final l’ is an unspecified singular object.

cautionOverrides.from: The English source glosses “me / myself” and “you / yourself” are broad. Reflexive meaning belongs to separate uses; here me and te refer to recipients. Lui/leur differ from Spanish le/les; do not add the named recipient after the pronoun in formal beginner models.
cautionOverrides.to: Here me and te mark recipients. Reflexive meaning belongs to other constructions. Use either “je donne un livre à Ana” or “je lui donne un livre” in beginner practice.
